Biotechnology for animal health

Bioactive proteins designed to protect the animals that feed the world

Knotide Bio designs, develops and advances highly stable bioactive small proteins for animal health, nutrition and welfare. To do so, we combine computational design, experimental discovery and cost-efficient production through precision fermentation, always with the species that anchor global food production in mind: aquaculture, poultry, swine, ruminants and pets.

Starting point

A well-characterised problem in aquaculture, under urgent regulatory pressure

Shrimp and salmon aquaculture face pathogens for which the available solutions are becoming increasingly ineffective, costly or prone to resistance. Vibrio parahaemolyticus, the causative agent of AHPND (Acute Hepatopancreatic Necrosis Disease), can collapse an entire shrimp pond within 30 days of stocking, and there is still no dominant biotechnological alternative to antibiotics. Sea lice (Lepeophtheirus salmonis and Caligus rogercresseyi), which affect salmon aquaculture, pose a comparable challenge and are the platform's next application.

This is where Knotide Bio starts. Our aim is to show, on a real and measurable problem, how a well-engineered biomolecule can replace approaches that have been worn down by resistance and regulatory rejection.

An industry under regulatory and economic pressure

Since 2010, AHPND has cost the global shrimp industry more than $43 billion, with mortality reaching up to 100% within 30-35 days of an outbreak. At the same time, EU and US import rejections over antibiotic residues, together with the EU's Farm to Fork target of -50% antimicrobial use by 2030, are driving active demand for residue-free alternatives.

Platform

From bioactive small proteins to product, with scientific rigour at every stage

Knotide Bio explores families of bioactive small proteins as the starting point for designing biotechnological solutions aimed at specific targets in animal health.

  1. 01

    Discovery

    Bioprospecting and selection of bioactive proteins with potential activity against identified targets.

  2. 02

    Characterisation

    Study of the structure, function and mechanism of action of the selected proteins.

  3. 03

    Validation

    Laboratory assays and analyses that confirm activity, selectivity and safety.

  4. 04

    Application

    Formulation and integration of the validated bioactive proteins into solutions for animal health, nutrition and welfare.

Integrated molecular discovery

Knotide Bio combines AI-guided molecular design with proprietary discovery libraries to develop small, highly stable bioactive proteins. These complementary technologies can be used on their own or together, which makes the discovery, engineering and optimisation of molecules tailored to specific biological applications more efficient.

Scalable and cost-efficient production

Our bioactive proteins are designed not only for biological performance but also for efficient production through precision fermentation.

This manufacturing approach is intended to enable scalable, consistent and cost-effective production and, in turn, to support applications where price is critical, such as aquaculture and livestock health.

Three complementary pillars in animal production

01

Animal health

Small proteins directed at parasites and pathogens relevant to animal production, offering an alternative to resistance-prone solutions.

Bioactive proteins applied in nutritional solutions that support animal performance and gut health.

03

Species the platform is built to serve

Illustrative example

In our lead application, a Knotide Bio protein is designed to neutralise the toxin that a pathogen needs to damage its host, instead of relying on broad antimicrobial activity. We are extending this approach to other pathogens, targets and species within the platform.

Knotide Bio's first application case is AHPND in shrimp aquaculture, chosen for its regulatory urgency, its market size and a well-characterised molecular target. Sea lice in salmon aquaculture is the platform's second application, and it shares the same core mechanism and the administration routes already used by the industry.

Mechanism of action: the designed protein blocker prevents the toxin complex from binding the cell-surface receptor.

Biosensing

Biosensing and molecular detection

The same bioactive small proteins engineered to recognise specific biological targets, such as toxins, bacteria, enzymes, fungi and viruses, can also act as the molecular recognition element in biosensing and rapid-detection formats.

01

Molecular recognition

Designed proteins that bind a defined target with high selectivity, serving as the sensing element in detection assays.

02

Stability by design

Highly stable proteins suited to the demanding conditions of field and production environments.

03

Rapid detection

A foundation for fast, protein-based detection of pathogens and biomarkers relevant to animal production.

04

Emerging application

An exploratory direction of the Knotide Bio platform, which we are advancing with the same scientific rigour as our animal-health programmes.

Knotide Bio brings together a multidisciplinary founding team whose expertise spans molecular microbiology, biomolecule engineering, biochemical engineering and industrial innovation. The team has experience across the full R&D pathway, from scientific concept and early discovery through development and validation, all the way to industrial implementation.

Together, the founders have led and managed R&D programmes across national and European funding instruments, including FCT, Horizon Europe and COMPETE2020/2030. They also bring direct experience in translating research into industrial innovation and commercial outcomes.

The founding team maintains strong links with academic and research institutions, including the Universities of Porto, Coimbra and Algarve and their research and innovation ecosystems, as well as collaborations with international academic and industrial organisations. At Knotide Bio, these complementary capabilities converge on a common objective: to engineer and develop bioactive molecules with the potential to deliver next-generation solutions for disease prevention and treatment.
